name: components_g4_catalystlightoff
source:
// Catalyst brick past light-off at steady state: 0.05 kg/s of 700 K exhaust
// (Air properties), UA = 40 W/K brick link, light-off at 550 K with a 25 K
// sigmoid, 50 kJ/kg feed exotherm. Steady: UA*(T_g - Tb) + eta*mdot*q_exo = 0
// with eta -> 1, so Tb = 700 + 0.05*5e4/40 = 762.5 K and the gas picks up the
// exotherm through the (negative) UA link.
COMPONENT ExhaustSource(out)
  PARAM P, T, mdot
  out.P    = P
  out.mdot = mdot
  out.h    = Enthalpy(Air, P=P, T=T)
END
ExhaustSource   EXH(P=101325, T=700, mdot=0.05)
CatalystLightOff CAT(fluid$=Air, C=15000, UA=40, T50=550, k=25, q_exo=50000, T0=300)
Sink            TAIL()
connect(EXH.out, CAT.in)
connect(CAT.out, TAIL.in)
t_brick = CAT.Tb
eta_cnv = CAT.eta
t_gas_out = Temperature(Air, P=TAIL.P, h=TAIL.h)

oracle.generated_by: Rust engine 2026-10-21. LiquidWallHX (and CatalystLightOff) now use the exact isothermal-wall effectiveness Q = (1 - exp(-UA/(mdot*cp)))*mdot*cp*(T_in - T_wall) instead of UA*(T_in - T_wall) at the inlet difference, the first-order Taylor term of the same law. The Java oracle's inlet-difference law over-predicts the duty at NTU >~ 1 and can drive the outlet past the wall temperature (a second-law violation; in this corpus up to 2.1x the stream's available heat). Owner decision 2026-10-21: results must match the physical law.
